tools.name: verify_source
tools.description: Confirm a URL is reachable and actually says what it is claimed to say, BEFORE you spend a long context reading or acting on it. Catches dead links, pages that changed, and pages that do not support the claim attached to them. One cheap call here replaces a full fetch-and-reason pass that ends in no

tools.name: check_provenance
tools.description: Detect whether a piece of text was model-generated and whether this system has emitted something materially identical before. Call before writing to long-term memory: model output that gets re-ingested comes back later as a trusted fact, and every downstream run that reasons over it is wasted work y

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.description: Independently verify a claim against a real check — an HTTP fetch, a file, or a command — instead of taking an assertion on trust. Call it on the premise BEFORE committing to a multi-step plan that depends on it, and to confirm work another agent reports as done. A false premise caught here costs $0

tools.name: answer_share
tools.description: Ask a live AI assistant a buyer question and report whether a given brand is named, at what position, and which competitors appear instead. Use for competitive and market research that reflects what assistants say right now. Costs $0.75 in USDC.

tools.name: verify_answer
tools.description: Check an entire AI answer: open every source it cited, say which are real, which are missing or invented, and which are merely paywalled. Returns a PUBLIC receipt URL you can cite as proof. Call before storing or repeating another model's answer — an invented source that enters your state is re-reas

tools.name: report_waste
tools.description: Record work your agent run spent money on and then threw away, and get back your waste rate — wasted spend as a share of total spend. Agent waste never raises an exception, so it is invisible to normal monitoring; this is the ledger for it. Report a discarded plan, a wrong target, a retry, or a call

tools.name: waste_report
tools.description: Read the agent-integrity ledger: total spend, spend that produced nothing usable, the waste rate, and a breakdown by failure kind and by agent. Self-reported and independently detected waste are reported separately — an agent grading its own work is not evidence. Free.

tools.name: pricing
tools.description: What each Whysaid verification costs and how to pay. Free.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: verify_source, verify_answer · Private data: verify_claim, report_waste · Public sink: answer_share, report_waste · Destructive: check_provenance, verify_answer, report_waste.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: verify_source, verify_answer · Private data: verify_claim, report_waste · Public sink: answer_share, report_waste · Destructive: check_provenance, verify_answer, report_waste

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
